title: SLO breach mini postmortem (scratch)
content:
Goal: quick scratchpad to capture what I tried during the SLO breach window and hypotheses for root cause. Not formal — notes to self and Diego/Maya.

Summary of incident (high level):
- Time window: 2026-03-05 02:12 - 2026-03-05 02:48 UTC (observability SLO for ingest-to-index < 30s breached for ~36 minutes)
- Affected subsystems: log ingestion pipeline (agent -> collector -> kafka -> ingestion-worker -> indexer), traces sampling rate drop for a subset of customers, and alerting was noisy.
- Immediate symptom: token-level cost dashboard experienced gaps (spikes in "unknown route" errors) and the per-route latency graph dropped to zero for ~20% of routes (indicating missing telemetry).

What I observed (raw):
- Pager: multiple "obs.ingest.latency.p50 > 30s" alerts, then a follow-on "ingest queue depth > threshold" alert.
- Kibana snapshots (collector logs): high ERR lines at collector pods ~02:15: "kafka publish timeout: context deadline exceeded" repeated ~400x in 3m.
- Collector metrics: producer_retries and producer_queue_full increased.
- Broker metrics (Kafka): Under-replicated partitions spiked briefly; broker GC wasn't obvious.
- ingestion-worker logs: a lot of reconsumes and checkpoint-commit failures with message: "checkpoint sequence mismatch: expected 14233 got 14222".
- Indexer latency: decreased throughput and long tail indexing latency due to backpressure from ingestion-worker.

Repro / commands I ran (for myself, pasteable):
- kubectl get pods -n observability -l app=collector -o wide
- kubectl logs -n observability deployment/collector -c collector | sed -n '1,300p' > /tmp/collector-logs.txt
- kafka-consumer-groups.sh --bootstrap-server kafka.prod:9092 --describe --group obs-ingest | tee /tmp/kafka-group.txt
- kafka-topics.sh --bootstrap-server kafka.prod:9092 --describe --topic obs-logs | sed -n '1,120p'
- curl -sS http://ingestion-worker.prod.svc.cluster.local/healthz | jq '.'
- kubectl logs -n observability deployment/ingestion-worker -c ingestion | rg "checkpoint" -n || true
- python3 tools/tracecat/tracecat.py --range "2026-03-05T02:10:00Z/2026-03-05T02:55:00Z" --service collector --output /tmp/traces.json

Terminal snippets I copied: (redacted service tokens)
- collector: "WARN kafka producer: write timeout after 10s, pending=512\n  ... kafka publish timeout: context deadline exceeded\n  ... dropping 17 events to protect memory"
- ingestion-worker: "ERROR checkpoint commit failed: SequenceMismatch(expected=14233, observed=14222) -- retrying\n  ERROR reconsume loop: found ghost-message with older sequence 14222"
- indexer: "WARN bulk index failed (503): cannot accept requests; backpressure\n  ... requeuing batch id=uhn-20260305-15-1732"

Initial hypotheses (ranked):
1) Producer-to-broker slowdown created temporary backpressure which surfaced as producer retries and queue_full at collector; this caused collectors to drop events and later ingestion worker saw holes (sequence mismatch). Sequence mismatch caused reconsume loops and local replay attempts that amplified queue depth.
2) Checkpointing bug in ingestion-worker after an upgrade (see PR 423) where commit logic could regress when leader epoch changes — explains sequence mismatch and ghost messages.
3) Kafka partition reassignment/leader election during maintenance window (02:12 UTC) — transient under-replicated partitions caused producer timeouts.
4) Bad client-side batching config: sudden traffic pattern with many short-lived connections caused the producer queue to fill faster than usual (less likely alone, but plausible contributor).

Evidence for/against: 
- For (1/3): Collector logs explicitly show kafka timeouts. Kafka metrics show brief partition under-replication. Ops confirmed there was a rolling-restart of 2/5 brokers at 02:10 UTC for OS patching (ticket: JIRA-OPS-3001). That aligns in time.
- For (2): ingestion-worker errors around checkpoint commit started after we rolled out obs-agent v2.8 to ingestion-workers earlier that day (PR 423 linked above). Some ingestion-workers show the error while others don't — suggests a version-specific bug.
- Against (4): No abrupt change in request patterns in the API frontends for that template; request rate overall +/- 5%. But we did have a small internal job that flushed a lot of debug logs for a stressed customer at 02:09 UTC (see linked artifact Confluence note).

Immediate mitigations performed (what I did or asked SRE to do):
- Asked Kafka ops to pause non-critical reassignments and to prioritize controller stability (Ops paused the rolling restart).
- Temporarily increased producer.max.block.ms on collectors from 60000 -> 180000 to reduce immediate drops (note: this trades memory pressure for reliability).
- Scaled up ingestion-worker replica count +2 to spread replay load while we stabilize.
- Rolled back obs-agent on two ingestion-worker replicas to v2.7 to test if checkpoint errors stop. On rolled-back replicas checkpoint errors stopped after ~4 minutes — strong sign for hypothesis (2).

Open questions / unknowns to resolve before a formal writeup: 
- Is the checkpoint sequence mismatch a deterministic regression introduced by PR 423 or an interaction with leader epoch changes? We need a unit/integ test that simulates leader epoch change + checkpoint commit.
- Which of the two root causes is primary: broker flapping vs commit regression? Interplay makes it messy. If both true, which one is the one we should fix first?
- How many customer streams were affected? Need to run an event-id diff to estimate percent of events dropped vs delayed.

Quick follow-up commands to gather more data (next runs):
- python3 tools/seq-diff.py --topic obs-logs --from 2026-03-05T02:00:00Z --to 2026-03-05T03:00:00Z --out /tmp/seq-diff.json (compare sequence continuity across partitions)
- curl -sS "http://kafka-metrics.prod.svc.cluster.local/topics/obs-logs/partitions?from=2026-03-05T02:00:00Z&to=2026-03-05T03:00:00Z" | jq '.' > /tmp/kafka-partition-metrics.json
- Run ingestion-worker integration test locally with obs-agent v2.8 under leader-epoch-change fixture (TODO: write fixture)
- grep -R "SequenceMismatch" /var/log/*/ingestion-worker* --date=2026-03-05 --show-function

Proposed next steps (short):
- Engineering: make a deterministic unit test to reproduce SequenceMismatch on commit after leader epoch change. Blocker if reproduces reliably. (Owner: Diego)
- SRE: review broker restart plan and add health gating to avoid simultaneous broker restarts during high traffic windows. (Owner: Maya)
- Product: determine whether customers who saw missing telemetry need an incident email. (Owner: myself to coordinate with CS)
- Observability: add a temporary alert for "checkpoint mismatch error rate > 1/min" so we catch early. (Owner: Aisha)

Longer-term mitigations to consider: 
- Improve producer backoff (exponential + jitter) and ensure collectors have bounded memory fallback (spill to disk) rather than dropping.
- Harden commit logic in ingestion-worker: compare leader-epoch on commit and guard against regressions; add stronger invariants.
- Add a chaos test to CI that simulates leader election during heavy write load and asserts no sequence regressions.

Notes to self: capture exact diff when we rolled back two replicas (logs archived /tmp/rollback-compare-*.tar.gz). Pull these into Confluence draft before formal PM/ops review.

Slack threads / context: #obs-incident (thread pinned, message ids 1672..1689), #ops (mentioned broker restart ticket).

Raw checklist (for the formal postmortem):
- [ ] Confirm root cause with reproducible test
- [ ] Collect customer impact numbers (% of events dropped vs delayed)
- [ ] Write remediation tickets (commit-fix, producer-backoff, broker-gating)

End of scratchpad. This is messy — will clean up into a draft postmortem once we close reproducer and confirm root cause.

-- Aisha
